entries.title: CLI update: block-operations

acceptedPr.title: perf(cli): scan only the tag seam when appending stream text
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## What

The text streaming path in `cli/src/utils/block-operations.ts` concatenated the whole accumulated block with each incoming delta and then ran two `String.includes` scans over the result:

```ts
const combinedText = lastBlock.content + text
if (combinedText.includes(THINK_OPEN_TAG) || combinedText.includes(THINK_CLOSE_TAG)) { ... }
```

That made one reply cost **O(n²) in its own length** — every delta re-walked everything before it, allocating and flattening the concatenation each time.

## Why it's safe to narrow the scan

A think tag can only be *completed* by the delta that completes it, at the seam between the block's tail and that delta. A tag already sitting inside the block was split out when it arrived. So the check now:

1. looks at the last 7 characters of the block (the widest partial tag, `</think`), plus the delta itself;
2. falls back to the original full-block scan whenever either contains `<`.

`<` in ordinary prose (`a < b`) still takes the full path, so nothing is lost.

## Measurement (`bun`, same machine, before → after)

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 8,000 deltas, 470 KB, plain text | 434 ms | **1.1 ms** |
| 4,000 deltas, 234 KB | 117 ms | **0.9 ms** |
| 2,000 deltas, 117 KB | 34 ms | **0.7 ms** |
| 1,000 deltas, 59 KB | 21 ms | **0.4 ms** |
| 8 subagents × 600 deltas | 38 ms | **5.5 ms** |

Cost is now linear in stream length instead of quadratic (`us/delta` was rising 17 → 54 as the stream grew; it now sits flat below 0.5).

Memory: no leak found on this path. The batched updater's interval is already disposed when a turn ends (`use-send-message.ts`), so it was not changed.

## Verification

- **Behavioural equivalence, not just tests:** 432 corpus scenarios (18 texts × 12 chunk sizes, root and agent paths) dumped from both implementations — **byte-identical** output, sha256 `6e06dde1…`.
- `bun test src/utils src/hooks` — **2672 pass, 0 fail** (157 files).
- `bun run typecheck` — exit 0.
- New `block-operations-streaming.test.ts` covers tags split inside the tag syntax at every seam position, the 7-char `</think` boundary, and long blocks keeping every character.

One pre-existing quirk surfaced while writing the tests and is left untouched: `<think></think>` with no content emits zero blocks, and a tag arriving after a long prefix folds the prefix into the reasoning block. Both behave identically before and after this change, hence the narrower assertions in the new test file.

ai.title: CLI root stream text delta scan narrowed to tag seam
ai.summary: The CLI streaming text path in `cli/src/utils/block-operations.ts` now detects think tags by scanning only the last 7 characters of the preceding block plus the new delta, instead of re-walking the entire accumulated block on every token. In `cli/src/utils/message-updater.ts`, `appendRootText` was added so the batched updater queues `RootTextDelta` objects and merges consecutive deltas of the same type into one block-array copy at the next flush, reducing allocation overhead during fast streams. These changes make the per-delta cost linear rather than quadratic while preserving identical block output, as verified by new tests that compare chunked and whole-text appends.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/utils/block-operations.ts`, the think-tag detection in `appendTextWithThinkParsingToBlocks` now computes a `seam` from the last `THINK_CLOSE_TAG.length - 1` characters of the block plus the delta instead of concatenating the entire block, and `cli/src/utils/message-updater.ts` adds `appendRootText` that queues `RootTextDelta` objects and merges consecutive same-type deltas into a single block-array copy per flush.

eli5.text: The terminal app now checks for thinking markers in incoming text only where the new piece meets the previous one, instead of re-scanning the entire reply every time a small chunk arrives. This is an internal performance tweak that reduces the work the app does while a long answer is still being typed out. You will not see any new features, and the text that appears in your chat remains exactly the same.

testNames: strips the run state older builds copied into message metadata

acceptedPr.title: cli: stop storing the turn's run state in chat message metadata
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## What

Each completed turn attached the **entire final `RunState`** to its AI message under `metadata.runState` (`cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts`). Nothing ever reads it back — a grep for `metadata?.runState` outside tests returns zero hits.

## Cost

After N turns, the chat store and `chat-messages.json` hold **N full snapshots** whose individual size grows with N: **O(N²)** in RAM and in every checkpoint's `JSON.stringify`. In a long session (30+ turns, ~25 MB mid-session snapshot) that's hundreds of MB retained and re-serialized on every checkpoint drain.

## Change

Drop the payload from `markComplete`. The type field stays, deprecated rather than removed: transcripts persisted by older versions carry the key, and the load path only `JSON.parse`s + shape-checks the messages array, so a stale field is safely ignored.

## Safety

- No production reader exists (grep-verified); the only assertion was in `use-send-message.test.tsx` and is removed with the write.
- The authoritative live state is `chatStore.runState`, set separately (`use-send-message.ts`); resume-on-error flows go through the checkpoint path (`scheduleCheckpointSave`), not this field.

## Tests

`bun run typecheck` clean; full `bun test` — 4332 pass / 46 skip / 0 fail (same totals as `main`).

ai.title: CLI drops turn run state from message metadata
ai.summary: The CLI no longer writes the full `RunState` object into `ChatMessage.metadata.runState` when a chat turn completes, removing the payload from `updater.markComplete` in `cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts`. To handle transcripts persisted by older versions, `sanitizeRestoredMessages` in `cli/src/utils/send-message-helpers.ts` now explicitly strips `runState` from message metadata during restore, preventing the stale field from being re-persisted on the next save. This change addresses the quadratic memory growth in `chat-messages.json` and RAM caused by accumulating duplicate run state snapshots in long sessions.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts`, the `updater.markComplete` call no longer passes `metadata: { runState }`; in `cli/src/utils/send-message-helpers.ts`, `sanitizeRestoredMessages` now checks for `'runState' in message.metadata` and strips it alongside `allowInlineAds` via destructuring.

eli5.text: The terminal assistant no longer saves a duplicate internal progress report inside each chat message when a turn finishes. This change affects anyone using the Freebuff or Codebuff terminal interface, reducing the amount of memory the app uses and the size of the saved chat history file as you work. You will not see a difference in how the assistant responds, but long sessions may feel more responsive over time because the app spends less effort managing this data.
